extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties and counsel involved in PTAB inter partes review proceedings (petitioner/patent owner)
extracted.subtask_short: PTAB director review of IPR denial
extracted.subtask_description: Review of a PTAB Decision Denying Institution on Director Review / Delegated Review Panel addressing (1) whether the Board engaged in implicit claim construction and (2) whether the Board properly considered petitioner's prior-art arguments. Focused on claim construction, prior-art mapping, and procedural sufficiency of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard — reasonable likelihood of prevailing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may deny institution if the Petition fails to establish a reasonable likelihood that Petitioner would prevail in showing unpatentability of the challenged claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior Decision denied institution because the Petition did not sufficiently show Mitchell meets the limitation 'propagating failure information by the detecting node to each node of the other nodes...'. The Decision evaluated whether Petitioner presented sufficient evidence and explanation to meet the reasonable-likelihood threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether the Board engaged in implicit claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the Board implicitly construed the disputed claim limitation (here, 'propagating failure information by the detecting node to each node of the other nodes') and, if so, whether that implicit construction was correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director/DRP reviews whether the original panel's analysis effectively construed the claim even if not labeled a 'claim construction.' The DRP found there was an implicit construction and that it was proper in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain and ordinary meaning may be inadequate (O2 Micro standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination that a claim term 'needs no construction' or has the 'plain and ordinary meaning' may be inadequate when the term has more than one 'ordinary' meaning or when reliance on a term's 'ordinary' meaning does not resolve the parties' dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parties disagree about the meaning of claim language, simply stating 'plain and ordinary meaning' is insufficient; the Board may need to resolve the dispute (and that resolution may amount to claim construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim language controls — read 'each node' / 'all other nodes' broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: When claim language recites 'each node' or 'all other nodes' without limiting language, those terms should be read broadly to encompass all nodes (upstream and downstream), unless the specification or prosecution history requires otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DRP agreed the claim words ('each node'/'all other nodes') do not specify upstream/downstream and thus support a construction including all nodes. The presence of 'each'/'all' was read literally to include every node traversed by the set of links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specification and prosecution history in claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult the specification and prosecution history to resolve claim-meaning disputes; statements in the specification and applicant's prosecution remarks can support a broad or narrow construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification's description of propagating a remote fault indication to 'the other nodes' and prosecution statements describing 'sending a failure information message to all the other nodes' supported the DRP's broad construction. Prosecution distinctions (e.g., contrasting Grenier's single-selector-node behavior) also inform construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must map each claim element to prior art (37 C.F.R. § 42.104(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must 'specify where each element of the claim is found in the prior art patents or printed publications relied upon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board is not required to develop undeveloped arguments for a petitioner. If a petitioner fails to make clear mappings or to develop an argument in the Petition, the Board may disregard implied or undeveloped positions. The Decision cites 37 C.F.R. § 42.104(b)(4) and admonishes that arguments cannot be buried or only hinted at.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency to extend prior-art teaching — must explain obviousness of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: To rely on a prior-art reference that teaches a narrower practice (e.g., downstream-only propagation), a petitioner must provide sufficient reasoning showing why a person of ordinary skill would have found it obvious to modify or extend that teaching to cover the claimed broader practice (e.g., propagation to each/all nodes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior Decision found Petitioner's showing insufficient to extend Mitchell's downstream-only propagation to the claim's requirement of propagation to each/all nodes. Petitioner must explain the rationale for the extension and why it would have been obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of modified prior art must be grounded in the Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that rely on a 'modified' version of a prior-art reference must be clearly presented and supported in the Petition for the Board to properly consider them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Board considered Petitioner's scenario of a failure 'far upstream' as presented, the DRP emphasized that new or further-developed positions presented for the first time in a Director Review request cannot be treated as having been before the original panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-instance showing can suffice for unpatentability (precedential case law), but must be presented timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Circuit precedent recognizes that a single instance that meets the plain language of a claim can be sufficient to render the claim unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner cited cases (Hewlett‑Packard, Unwired Planet, etc.) in the Request, but because those legal arguments were not presented in the original Petition/Prelim. Resp., the original panel could not have misapprehended them. Legal standards can be dispositive but must be argued in the record before the deciding panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may rely on expert declarations but they must tie to the reference disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony (e.g., declarations) is a permissible evidentiary tool to interpret what the prior art teaches, but it must be clearly connected to the prior-art disclosure and the petitioner's arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior Decision reviewed Dr. Houh's testimony alongside the Mitchell reference and parties' arguments. Declarations that assert teachings beyond the text/figures must still demonstrate a reasonable basis in the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of implicit claim construction to resolve dispositive issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board panel may implicitly construe claims (i.e., resolve the parties' dispute over claim meaning) when required to decide dispositive issues even if the panel does not label the discussion as formal 'claim construction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DRP stated nothing improper in a panel resolving the dispositive issue through implicit construction; panels are not required to formally designate every resolution as a 'claim construction' so long as the resolution is reasoned and consistent with law and record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Director Review / Delegated Review Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Review (or delegated DRP review) is limited to the issues the Director ordered reviewed — here, (1) whether the Board engaged in an implicit claim construction and if so whether correct; and (2) whether the Board properly considered Petitioner's argument that Mitchell reads on the propagating-failure limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DRP's authority and analysis conform to the Director's order; review is focused on the ordered questions and does not expand to newly-raised arguments outside the scope or not properly before the original panel.
